title: Video placement on stage: VideoDisplayObject model, stage UI, and compiler integration
description:
## Problem

Task 0760 added `File > Import > Import Video...` which stores a `VideoItem` in the library. But there is no way to place video content onto the stage:

1. No `VideoDisplayObject` type exists in the engine model (`packages/core/src/engine/types.ts`). The `DisplayObject` union is `ShapeDisplayObject | SymbolInstance | DrawingObject | TextDisplayObject | BitmapDisplayObject | GroupObject` — video is absent.
2. `handleStageDrop` in `Shell.tsx` handles bitmap and symbol items from library drag; video items are silently ignored (no matching branch).
3. The SWF compiler auto-places ALL VideoItems at `(0, 0)` at depth 50000+, regardless of model (hard-coded in `compile.ts` lines 644–660). The position/layer is not user-controllable.
4. The canvas renderer has no video preview — dragging a video to the stage shows nothing.

## What to implement

### 1. `VideoDisplayObject` model type

Add to `packages/core/src/engine/types.ts`:
```ts
export interface VideoDisplayObject {
  readonly type: "video";
  readonly id: string;
  readonly libraryItemId: string;   // → VideoItem.id
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly height: number;
  readonly instanceName?: string;
}
```
Add to the `DisplayObject` union. Add `createVideo()` factory (or extend the existing one) in `packages/core/src/model/library.ts`.

### 2. Stage drag-and-drop from library

In `Shell.tsx handleStageDrop`: when the dragged item has `itemType === "video"`, create a `VideoDisplayObject` using the VideoItem's `width`/`height`, add it to the active frame timeline, and record it in the doc.

### 3. Canvas renderer preview

In `packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts`, handle `displayObj.type === "video"`: draw a placeholder (e.g., dark rectangle with a ▶ icon / first-frame thumbnail if available) so the video footprint is visible on the authoring stage.

### 4. SWF compiler integration

Replace the hard-coded "place all VideoItems at (0,0)" logic in `compile.ts` with model-driven placement:
- Only emit `DefineVideoStream` + `PlaceObject2` for VideoItems that have at least one `VideoDisplayObject` referencing them in the scene.
- Use the `VideoDisplayObject.x/y/width/height` for the PlaceObject2 matrix.
- Assign depth through the normal depth-assignment system so video respects layer order.

### 5. MCP agent tool

Extend `stage_place_instance` (or add a dedicated `stage_place_video`) in `registry.ts` to accept a VideoItem ID and place a VideoDisplayObject on the active layer/frame.

## Acceptance criteria

- Drag a VideoItem from the library to the stage: a VideoDisplayObject appears at the drop coordinates.
- Select and reposition the VideoDisplayObject; the published SWF places the video at the new position.
- Unit tests: `VideoDisplayObject` round-trips through `saveFla`/`loadFla`.
- E2E (optional): publish a SWF with a positioned VideoItem and assert PlaceObject2 matrix matches the model coords.

## Files

- `packages/core/src/engine/types.ts` — add VideoDisplayObject
- `packages/core/src/model/library.ts` — add model helpers if needed
- `packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx` — handleStageDrop video branch
- `packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts` — video preview
- `packages/swf/src/compile.ts` — model-driven video placement
- `packages/authoring-ui/src/agent/registry.ts` — MCP stage_place_instance or new tool
